key_insight: DuSS-PET reconstructs low-dose PET images without paired low- and full-dose training scans by enforcing consistency between images and image-derived pseudo-sinograms.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support lower-dose PET imaging while reducing reliance on paired training data, but clinical utility remains to be established.
method: Uses computational Noisier2Noise training with Bernoulli corruption to approximate low-count noise.
Combines adaptive Swin transformer pseudo-sinogram restoration with plug-and-play image enhancement.
Enforces self-supervised consistency between image and pseudo-sinogram representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports multi-center evaluation across dose levels and scanner vendors, outperforming other self-supervised methods and matching or exceeding fully supervised approaches, without providing quantitative results.
watch_item: Image-derived pseudo-sinograms approximate acquisition data; preservation of quantitative PET measurements and diagnostic findings requires clinical validation.
paper_title: DuSS-PET: Self-Supervised Low-Dose PET Reconstruction Using Pseudo-Dual-Domain Consistency Without Paired Data
